reviews.Sofia: Works: one continuous outline, both lines leave the start heading right, big S-neck reads as a swan, no detached eye. Change: keep the neck curves gentle with no sharp kinks, and make the two lines meet cleanly at the beak tip. Keep strokes long, as few joins as possible. Optional: a small tail point at the left would help.
reviews.Omar: Nice, I like it. Two lines from the tail leave START about 75 degrees apart, so that's fine, and no floating bits. One fix: where the upper line comes off the back and turns up into the neck, the corner is too tight. Round it into a smooth sweep, a bit more room before it heads up, or the fall stops there. Same on the head: keep the turn into the beak soft. The two lines meeting at the beak tip is fine. If you can, make the neck a touch longer and more S-shaped so it reads swan, not duck. Otherwise good to lock. Sofia and I can take one line each, and I'll take the start.
reviews.Jack: Body and two-line split from the tail work well. Change: make the neck slimmer, taller and more S-curved (it reads duck-like now), keep head small with a clear beak pointing right, lift the tail tip slightly. Client wants graceful and long-necked, no fish. Otherwise approve.
